reference.name: Email-based Password Reset
reference.description: Happy path: An unauthenticated user at the login prompt chooses the “Forgot Password?” path, submits their email to request a password reset, sees an email-sent confirmation, opens the reset-password interface (presented here as an in-app form), enters and confirms a new password, and then is returned to the login screen with a notification that the password was changed and they must re-authenticate. Entry point: login screen (password entry). Exit point: back to login screen, ready for the user to sign in with the new password. Assumptions: user is signed out (no active session), has access to the email address they submit, and is on a desktop-like split layout (left marketing panel, right auth panel). No additional authentication steps (2FA) are visible in these screens.
reference.problem:
Task: Recover access to an account by resetting a forgotten password.

- From the user's perspective: The user needs to regain access to their account. They expect to be able to request a password reset by providing their email, receive confirmation that an email has been sent, set a new password (enter and confirm), and then log in with the new password.

- From the interface/system perspective: The UI provides a 'Forgot Password?' entry on the login screen that navigates to an email-collection screen. After the email is submitted the interface shows a success notification. The system then presents a reset-password form where the user enters and confirms a new password. The UI enforces (visibly) entering both password fields and provides a Reset action. After reset the system provides feedback that the password changed and returns the user to the login prompt.

- End result:
  - User-perceived outcome: The user sees confirmation that the reset email was sent, successfully sets a new password, receives confirmation that the password changed, and is asked to log in again.
  - System-level outcome: The user’s password is updated and the session requires re-authentication (password change notification shown).

reference.problem: The user is trying to access Faire’s wholesale marketplace and get into an authenticated shopping experience. The screen shows a retail marketplace homepage with a centered promotional modal overlay. The overall design is warm, editorial, and commerce-focused, using a muted beige base combined with deep burgundy and brown accent tones. Accent tones in the marketplace branding and the modal imagery use warm ochre/gold around HEX #735517 and a deeper chestnut brown around HEX #522814. The modal itself has a cream/off-white body matching the site background, with a dark charcoal button around HEX #3A3A3A and white button text. The close icon is a small white “X” on the top-right of the modal image area. Navigation and secondary labels are rendered in low-contrast dark gray/brown for a refined, understated look.

Typography: the interface uses a mix of serif and sans-serif styling. The modal headline is a large elegant serif font, likely a display serif in the range of 28–36 px, with regular to medium weight and generous line height for a sophisticated editorial feel. Supporting body copy beneath is smaller, around 13–15 px, in a clean sans-serif, medium-gray color, left-aligned with comfortable spacing. The site header and navigation use a small to medium sans-serif font, around 12–14 px, with regular weight and tight but readable tracking. Section labels and category names are also sans-serif, with a restrained, utilitarian e-commerce tone.

Layout and structure: the base page uses a full-width top announcement bar, then a header row containing the brand mark on the left, category dropdown, search bar, and utility actions on the right. A secondary navigation row with category links sits below. The hero section spans the full width beneath the nav, with content on the left and a large abstract product illustration on the right. Over this, a centered modal appears as a vertical card with a fixed width and strong elevation. The modal is divided into two zones: a top image area showing stacked product/office items on a gold background, and a lower content area with headline, description, and CTA button. The modal is vertically centered and blocks interaction with the dimmed page underneath.

The modal panel has squared-off corners or a very subtle radius, with a thin shadow that lifts it from the background. The CTA button spans most of the modal width, centered horizontally, with dark fill, white label text, and a compact height of roughly 40–44 px. The close control sits in the upper-right corner of the modal image header, small and unobtrusive. Behind the modal, the hero banner includes a left-aligned logo lockup and a muted button, plus large rounded decorative shapes on the right. Lower on the page, partially visible category tiles/cards are arranged in a grid, each with a small thumbnail and label.

Visual style: the screen balances luxury editorial styling with marketplace utility. The modal uses a promotional campaign aesthetic, while the underlying homepage maintains a catalog-oriented structure. The dimmed overlay reduces visual noise and forces attention onto the pop-up offer. Spacing is generous, with soft shadows, warm neutrals, and subtle contrast rather than harsh borders. The interface feels polished, curated, and brand-forward.

No obvious animation is visible in the screenshot, but the modal likely appears with a fade-in or scale-up transition and a darkened overlay fade behind it, using standard ease-out motion for a smooth promotional interruption.

content.description:
The screen is a clean, editorial-style marketplace homepage for a craft/home-goods shopping platform. The visual tone is warm, premium, and lightly rustic, with a strong emphasis on product discovery. The overall composition uses a large white canvas (#FFFFFF) with a deep maroon promotional hero block and soft beige accents. The key accent palette appears to include burnt sienna / terracotta (#A3613C), dark wine brown (#511910), muted tan (#AF8A62), warm gray (#A39D94), and dusty peach (#D4A58E). These colors are used in banners, badges, and product imagery to create a handmade, boutique feel.

At the top is a thin announcement strip with centered promotional text in a small sans-serif font, dark gray/black on a very light cream background. Under it sits the main header: the FAIRE logo on the left in serif uppercase lettering, a category dropdown, a wide rounded search field with a magnifying-glass icon, then utility actions on the right such as market list, language selector, setup guide, notifications, account, and cart icons. These header elements are compact, horizontally aligned, and spaced evenly to support quick shopping navigation.

Below the header is a full-width hero banner with a dark maroon background (#511910). On the left, the banner contains the Faire Market logo lockup and a white marketing headline. Beneath it is a light button with subtle shadow and rounded corners, styled in an off-white fill with dark text, inviting users to shop special offers. On the right side of the hero is a large decorative product illustration in peach and orange tones (#D4A58E and a brighter coral/orange), partly cropped to the edge to create a bold, modern merchandising feel. The banner uses large negative space and strong contrast to emphasize the promotional message.

The main content area is organized into multiple stacked discovery sections. First is a personalized greeting and a 2-row grid of category tiles. Each tile is a pale cream rectangle with a small product thumbnail on the left and category text on the right. The typography here is simple and readable, likely a modern sans-serif around 13–16 px, medium weight for headings and regular weight for sublabels. Tiles use soft borders, minimal shadows, and a gentle beige background to feel approachable and editorial.

Further down, multiple product recommendation sections appear, such as “Recently viewed” and “Ideas for you.” These sections are arranged as horizontal rows or responsive grids of product cards. Each card contains a large square product image at the top, usually with small overlay badges in the upper-left corner like “New,” “Bestseller,” or “Trending” on white pill-shaped labels with dark text. In the upper-right corner of each card there is a heart/favorite icon. At the bottom corners of the image area, small circular action buttons appear: one with a magnifier/quick-view style icon and another with a plus symbol for adding/saving. Under the image, product metadata is stacked in a compact text block: price in bold dark text, MSRP in lighter gray with strikethrough when applicable, product name, brand/vendor, star rating, minimum order quantity or shipping threshold, and promotion notes. Some cards include tiny color swatches or small avatar-like dots indicating variants or social proof.

Typography across the marketplace content mixes elegant serif headings with clean sans-serif body text. Section titles like “Welcome to Faire” or “Recently viewed” use a refined serif font with larger size and high contrast, while product details and navigation use a neutral sans-serif. The hierarchy is achieved through size, weight, and spacing rather than heavy color use. Primary text is dark charcoal (#222222), secondary metadata is mid-gray (#A39D94), and promotional or discount labels use warm orange/terracotta tones.

Spacing is generous and modular. The page uses a centered content column with consistent horizontal margins and a large number of evenly spaced cards. The product grids are multi-column, likely 4–5 columns depending on viewport width, with cards aligned in rows and each card maintaining equal width and consistent gutters. The footer is minimal and airy, featuring a large callout to download the mobile app, app store badges, and two columns of company/explore links. Social icons sit nearby, and legal links appear in a small footer line at the bottom in muted gray.

Overall, the interface feels polished, marketplace-driven, and discovery-oriented, combining a curated editorial look with dense e-commerce browsing functionality. The color palette is warm, earthy, and brand-led, while the layout prioritizes product browsing, category exploration, and promotional merchandising.
content.layout:
The layout is a long vertically scrolling homepage built from stacked sections inside a centered content container. It starts with a thin announcement bar, then a single-row global header with multiple grouped controls: logo at left, navigation/search in the middle, account and utility actions at right. Below that is a full-width hero banner spanning the content area.

The main body uses a single-column page structure with multiple content blocks stacked vertically. The first block contains a heading and a 2-row by 4-column grid of category tiles. After that, product discovery sections appear as horizontally aligned multi-card grids. Each product section is arranged in repeated rows of 4–5 cards across, depending on available width, with each card maintaining consistent height and image-to-text proportions. Cards are organized in a clean modular grid with equal gutters and aligned baselines for pricing and metadata.

The page ends with a spacious footer area that splits into columns: an app promotion block on the left and link columns on the right, followed by a narrow legal footer line. The overall layout is content-dense but orderly, using strong vertical section spacing and a consistent card grid system.
content.functions:
Users can browse a marketplace of wholesale and artisan products, search for specific items, jump into categories, and explore curated recommendations. At the smallest interaction level, they can type in the search field, open the category dropdown, click category tiles, open product cards, favorite items with the heart icon, or use quick action buttons on cards such as view or add. They can also switch language, access the market list, open setup guidance, and use notification or account controls in the header.

At a broader workflow level, the interface supports discovery shopping: users can move from broad categories to specific products, compare products across recommendation rows, inspect pricing and minimums, and save items for later. The “Recently viewed” section helps users resume browsing, while “Ideas for you” and labeled badges like “Bestseller” and “Trending” help users evaluate relevance and popularity quickly. The footer also supports conversion by promoting the mobile app and offering company and support links.

At the highest level, the screen helps buyers discover and source products efficiently from a curated wholesale marketplace. It balances inspiration and utility, allowing users to explore merchandise, identify suitable suppliers, and take the first steps toward purchasing or saving products for business use.
